title: A Inheritance for the Cipher
premise: True-crime podcaster Zephyrine Vane has spent five years chronicling the 1971 disappearance of schoolteacher Odile Marsh, the coldest case in the fog-bound town of Grayhollow. When a descendant donates Odile's diary to Zephyrine's archive, they discover entries written years after her disappearance—proof she lived hidden, and proof someone silenced her again. As Zephyrine deciphers the diary's cipher, they realize the killer is still alive, still respected, and has been feeding them 'tips' to control the narrative. In the climax, Zephyrine stages a fake archive reveal to lure the killer into confessing on a live recording; the resolution sees the town forced to confront that its beloved founding family built its legacy on a buried body.
about_author: Kestrel Thornbury is the pen name of a former small-town archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's unfinished stories before writing their own. They live near the coast with two indifferent cats and an unhealthy interest in municipal records.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Missing
chapters.summary: Zephyrine Vane's POV. While preparing the final episode of their podcast on Odile Marsh's 1971 disappearance, Zephyrine receives the diary from Odile's estranged great-niece—and finds entries dated decades after she vanished. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the case Zephyrine thought was closed was never even open. A threatening note tucked in the diary's spine signals someone is watching.

chapters.title: Entries That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, intercut with diary excerpts. Decoding the cipher reveals Odile witnessed something in 1971—something involving the town's revered Aldous Crane family—and chose invisibility over testimony until fear of exposure caught up with her. Zephyrine notices the anonymous 'tips' they've received for years match details only the killer could know. The beat: loyalty to sources curdles into suspicion of everyone.

chapters.title: The Keeper of the File
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Following the diary's clues to a sealed parish annex, Zephyrine discovers the killer is Elias Crane, the elderly town historian who has curated the official record for fifty years—and who realizes, mid-conversation, how much Zephyrine has decoded. He offers partnership, then veiled threats against the great-niece. The beat: power revealed as patient, polite, and utterly corrupting.

chapters.title: A Confession, Recorded
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Announcing a final episode that will 'reveal' the full decoded diary, Zephyrine baits Elias into the archive at night, where hidden microphones capture his confession to silencing Odile twice—once with silence, once with murder. Police arrive as he tries to burn the originals. The beat: truth wins, but Zephyrine mourns the town that preferred its alphabetized lies.
